title.point: God gave us His commandments not just to tell us how to behave, but so we could know what He is really like!

lastWeekReview.title: The Children of Israel—God Feeding His People
bullets: The Israelites were hungry in the wilderness and started complaining again.
God promised, 'I will rain bread from heaven for you!'
Each morning tiny white flakes covered the ground — they called it MANNA ('What is it?').
They gathered just enough for one day; saved-up leftovers spoiled with worms!
God also sent QUAIL for meat, and for 40 years their clothes never wore out!
God knows what we need before we even ask — we can trust Him instead of complaining.
lastWeekReview.discussion: Did you try PRAYING first this week instead of worrying or complaining? What happened? Remember — God already knows what you need before you even ask Him!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: "…Your Father knows the things that you have need of before you ask Him." — Matthew 6:8

kidsContent.text: Three months after leaving Egypt, the children of Israel camped in the wilderness at the foot of a huge mountain — Mount Sinai.
God called Moses up the mountain and into His presence. There was thunder, lightning, thick smoke, and a loud trumpet blast — everyone knew that GOD was there!
There God gave Moses special words we call the Ten Commandments — or the Ten Words. They weren't just rules to boss people around.
God gave them so His people would know how to live — and even more, so they could know what HE is really like!
🌟 God's commandments are like a window: when we look at them, we get to see who God is!

image.caption: Moses meets God on Mount Sinai amid thunder and lightning

kidsContent.text: 1.  Have no other gods before Me.  —  God wants to be first in our hearts. He loves us and wants our love for Him alone.
2.  Do not make idols.  —  Nothing should take God's place: not toys, games, celebrities, or screens.
3.  Do not take God's name in vain.  —  His name is precious, not something to throw around carelessly (even saying 'OMG').
4.  Remember the Sabbath day.  —  God rested on the seventh day; He gives us a day to rest and remember that HE made everything.
5.  Honor your father and mother.  —  We came from our parents, and our parents came from God — He is the Source we all come from.
🌟 The first five commandments all show us how big, holy, and loving God is. Loving God always comes first!

lesson.practicePoint: This week, pick ONE of the first five commandments and keep it on purpose — then ask yourself, 'What does this teach me about God?' Be ready to share next week!

memoryVerse.text: If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
memoryVerse.application: Keeping God's commandments isn't about being 'good enough.' Jesus says it flows from love — when we truly love Him, we want to do what He says.

parts.text: Materials: 5 'stone tablet' cards (1–5), 5 'What it shows about God' cards, tape, a prize bag
Setup: Stick the five commandment cards on one wall and the five 'about God' cards (mixed up) on another.
Round 1 — Match-Up: In two teams, kids race to match each commandment to what it teaches about God (e.g. 'No other gods' → 'God wants to be first / He loves us').
Round 2 — Order It: Scramble the tablet cards; teams line them up 1–5 from memory. Fastest correct order wins!
Round 3 — Memory Verse Relay: Kids take turns adding one word of John 14:15 until the whole class says it together.
📖 Connection: God's rules are a window into His heart — keeping them helps us KNOW Him, not just obey Him.

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: The Israelite camp at the foot of Mount Sinai. Thunder rumbles; a thick cloud covers the mountain top.
Three months after leaving Egypt, God's people camped before a great mountain. Then God called Moses up to meet with Him.
Look at the mountain! Thunder, lightning, smoke — and listen, a trumpet getting LOUDER and louder!
I'm shaking! Is God really up there? What will He say to Moses?
Moses climbs up into the cloud. God begins to speak.
I am Jehovah your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. You shall have no other gods before Me.
No other gods… You want to be first in their hearts, because You love them!
Do not make idols. Do not take My name in vain. Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. Honor your father and your mother.
These words aren't only rules… every one of them shows the people what YOU are like!
Moses comes back down the mountain to the people.
Moses! What did God say? Are these just a long list of things we can't do?
No! God gave these Ten Words so we would know how to live — and even more, so we could know HIM. Loving God comes first!
So when I keep God's commandments, I'm getting to know what He is really like?
God's commandments are a window to His heart — if we love Him, we'll keep His Word!

description.text: Setup: Mark a 'base camp' start line and a 'mountain top' at the far end with a chair or cone.
Rules: One runner at a time climbs to the 'top,' grabs one 'commandment card' (1–5), and races it back to the team.
Goal: The team must collect all five cards AND lay them in the right order 1–5 to win.
Twist: Every time the leader shouts 'THUNDER!' everyone must freeze in awe for 3 seconds before running again.
📖 Connection: Moses climbed Mount Sinai to receive God's words — we're 'climbing' to gather them too!
Materials: Cones/chairs, five numbered cards per team
Setup: Kids spread out across the gym. One leader controls a whistle or 'trumpet' sound.
Rules: While music plays, kids move (hop, march, tiptoe as called). When the 'trumpet' blasts, everyone FREEZES — like the people before the holy mountain.
Elimination: Anyone who moves during a freeze does 5 jumping jacks and rejoins.
Sabbath Round: On 'Sabbath REST!' everyone sits and rests quietly for 10 seconds (commandment 4!).
📖 Connection: At Sinai the trumpet grew louder and the people stood in awe — God is holy and worthy of our reverence!
Materials: Whistle or horn, music player

movieViewing.title: Moses, God, and the Mountain
movieViewing.description: TBTMS story video — God calls Moses up Mount Sinai and gives His people the Ten Commandments. (Exodus 19–20)

description.text: Before kids arrive, hide ten 'stone tablet' cards around the outdoor area (five real first-commandments, five silly fakes like 'Never eat vegetables!').
Teams hunt for tablets and bring them back to 'Mount Sinai' (a marked base).
Sorting: Teams keep only the TRUE first-five commandments and toss out the fakes. Correct set = win!
Twist: For each real commandment, the team shouts one thing it shows us about God.
Materials: Ten tablet-shaped cards, a base marker

outdoor.tip: ⛰️ The commandments came from a mountain wrapped in thunder and glory — help kids feel that God is awesome and holy, and that His rules flow from His love for us.
